classification.difficultyReason: Construct triangles from three side lengths and from two equal legs with a specified included angle.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Use a ruler and compasses to construct a triangle with side lengths $6\text{ cm}$, $7\text{ cm}$ and $8\text{ cm}$.

answer.short: A triangle with sides $6\text{ cm}$, $7\text{ cm}$ and $8\text{ cm}$, with construction arcs retained.
answer.worked: Draw $AB=8\text{ cm}$. With centre $A$, draw an arc of radius $6\text{ cm}$. With centre $B$, draw an arc of radius $7\text{ cm}$ intersecting the first arc at $C$. Join $AC$ and $BC$, retaining the construction arcs. The radii give $AC=6\text{ cm}$ and $BC=7\text{ cm}$.

spec.description: Authored completed construction with an 8 cm base and intersecting compass arcs of radii 6 cm and 7 cm. Answer figure is illustrative; students construct at full size.
spec.mathematics: AB=8 cm, AC=6 cm and BC=7 cm. C is the upper intersection of the two construction circles.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Use a ruler, compasses and a protractor to construct an isosceles triangle with legs of length $6\text{ cm}$ and an apex angle of $110^\circ$.

answer.short: An isosceles triangle with equal legs $6\text{ cm}$ and included apex angle $110^\circ$.
answer.worked: Draw a circle with centre $A$ and radius $6\text{ cm}$. Choose a point $B$ on the circle and draw $AB$. Use a protractor to draw a ray from $A$ making $110^\circ$ with $AB$. Label its intersection with the circle $C$ and join $BC$. Since $AB$ and $AC$ are radii, both legs are $6\text{ cm}$, and $\angle BAC=110^\circ$.

spec.description: Authored completed isosceles construction using two radii of one circle and a protractor-measured included angle. Answer figure is illustrative; students construct at full size.
spec.mathematics: AB=AC=6 cm and angle BAC=110 degrees.
